when_to_use: Hammond B-3 organ trio/quintet, gospel-blues 12-bar, organ solo with a Leslie/drawbar dynamic arc, 65-145 BPM

defaults.feel: bluesy swung 8ths, thick backbeat laid behind the grid, organ bass pedal legato

signature_moves: gospel plagal cadence: Bb/F -> F7 (IV/I -> I)
12-bar gospel-blues turnaround: Gm7 -> C7(#9) -> F7 D7 -> Gm7 C7
diminished passing chord: Bb7 -> Bbdim7 -> F7
cadence_options: gospel plagal: IV -> I, or IV/I -> I
outro hold: land on 7#9 or 6/9, sustained with an organ glissando (palm smear)
avoid: dense ii-V chains or bebop-level harmonic motion - soul jazz stays on 12-bar gospel-blues, deliberately sparse (see soul-jazz-genre.md SS5-6)
a tight, precise big-band ride feel - the backbeat should sit behind the grid, not on it

hook_archetypes.name: organ-vamp-pedal
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a repeating bass-pedal figure the organ states alone before the band enters
hook_archetypes.contour: root-5th pedal under a simple chordal comp, Leslie set slow (chorale)

hook_archetypes.name: call-and-response-riff
hook_archetypes.rhythm: a 2-bar horn riff answered by a 2-bar organ comp fill
hook_archetypes.contour: tenor sax/trumpet state a bluesy unison phrase, organ answers with a gospel-tinged chordal fill

head.contour: singable unison/harmony line over the 12-bar form, gospel-inflected
head.placement: laid slightly behind the grid, matching the backbeat

organ-solo.note_lengths: phrases lengthen and thicken as the solo builds
organ-solo.contour: drawbars pulled out gradually, runs get faster and denser toward the peak
organ-solo.placement: pushes forward at the peak as the Leslie switches to fast tremolo

sax-guitar-solo.note_lengths: shorter, bluesier phrases, call-and-response with organ comping
sax-guitar-solo.contour: blues/gospel scale based, sub-tone or thumb-picked depending on instrument

head-return.note_lengths: back to the head's clear phrasing
head-return.placement: laid slightly behind the grid, matching the backbeat

drum_skeleton.low_energy: ride swung 8ths, thick snare backbeat on 2 and 4 laid behind the grid, hi-hat mostly closed
drum_skeleton.mid_energy: hi-hat opens on off-beat accents, kick more present under the organ pedal
drum_skeleton.high_energy: ride pushes harder, snare accents thicken under the organ or sax solo peak, hi-hat becomes sloshier

arrangement_defaults.layout_rules: organ states the intro vamp alone with Leslie slow; horns state the head with organ comping; organ solo builds by pulling drawbars and switching Leslie to fast at the peak; sax or guitar trades the foreground while organ returns to comping; head returns with full band; outro holds a 7#9 or 6/9 chord with an upward organ glissando

anti_boredom_rules: the organ solo must have a dynamic arc - drawbars and Leslie speed change across the solo
keep harmony on the sparse 12-bar gospel-blues vocabulary
the backbeat stays behind the grid at every energy level
the call-and-response riff returns varied by section or instrument
velocity is never flat across a voice within a bar

bass_behavior.rhythmic_relationship: locks with kick while sustaining gospel-blues root and fifth motion
bass_behavior.density: continuous but simple, adding passing tones only near peaks
bass_behavior.articulation: legato organ pedal or low drawbar tone

groove_intent.feel: bluesy swung-eighth pocket with a thick laid-back backbeat
groove_intent.kick: supports organ pedal and becomes more present at higher energy
groove_intent.hihat: closed early, sloshier on offbeat accents later
groove_intent.ensemble_relationship: organ pedal and drums create the pocket while horns and organ trade calls and responses

distinguishing_traits: Hammond registration and Leslie speed form the main dynamic arc
organ pedal replaces walking bass and supports a heavy behind-grid backbeat
